target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Previous D081 defines the scope of the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) for financial instruments measured at amortized cost and off-balance sheet exposures. Current D085 repeats this exact scope definition in P108 and expands on the methodology. They cover the same specific topic of ACL scope definition.

Previous D082 details the factors considered in determining the ACL, including macroeconomic forecasts (GDP, equity markets, unemployment) and the 13-quarter forecast period with reversion. Current D085 includes these same factors and the 13-quarter reversion in P109, serving as the counterpart for the methodology details.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citi uses the Current Expected Credit Losses (CECL) methodology under ASC 326 to estimate lifetime expected credit losses for financial assets carried at amortized cost, including held-for-investment loans and held-to-maturity debt securities, excluding those measured at fair value.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft and Citi define the Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) as an estimate of expected credit losses over the life of the instrument for financial assets carried at amortized cost. Microsoft specifies that this includes certain off-balance sheet exposures like HFI loans and lending commitments. Similarly, Citi defines the ACL under ASC 326 as a valuation account deducted from amortized cost assets to present the net amount management expects to collect over the expected life, explicitly covering held-for-investment loans and held-to-maturity debt securities, while excluding assets measured at fair value.

sentences.text: The ACL for financial instruments measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet exposures (e.g., HFI loans and lending commitments, HTM securities, customer and other receivables and certain guarantees) represents an estimate of expected credit losses over the entire life of the financial instrument.

ASC 326 defines the ACL as a valuation account that is deducted from the amortized cost of a financial asset to present the net amount that management expects to collect on the financial asset over its expected life.

The CECL methodology utilizes a lifetime expected credit loss (ECL) measurement objective for the recognition of credit losses for held-for-investment (HFI) loans, held-to-maturity (HTM) debt securities, receivables and other financial assets measured at amortized cost at the time the financial asset is originated or acquired.

comparisons.peer_topic: Allowance for Credit Losses Scope and Measurement Methodology
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm's allowance for credit losses applies to loans and lending commitments at amortized cost, measured collectively for similar risks via modeling or asset-specifically for unique risks, with scope excluding those at fair value.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures define the scope of the allowance for credit losses as applying to loans and lending commitments accounted for at amortized cost. Microsoft notes that the ACL covers these instruments and certain off-balance sheet exposures. Goldman Sachs explicitly states its allowance covers 'loans and lending commitments accounted for at amortized cost' and excludes those accounted for at fair value or lower of cost or fair value, aligning with the amortized cost focus of the peer disclosure.

sentences.text: The ACL for financial instruments measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet exposures (e.g., HFI loans and lending commitments, HTM securities, customer and other receivables and certain guarantees) represents an estimate of expected credit losses over the entire life of the financial instrument.
The firm's allowance for credit losses consists of the allowance for losses on loans and lending commitments accounted for at amortized cost.
Loans and lending commitments accounted for at fair value or accounted for at the lower of cost or fair value are not subject to an allowance for credit losses.

comparisons.peer_topic: Definition and composition of allowance for credit losses
comparisons.peer_summary: The allowance for credit losses represents management's estimate of expected credit losses over the remaining expected life of financial assets at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet commitments. It generally comprises the allowance for loan losses, the allowance for lending-related commitments, and the allowance for credit losses on investment securities.
comparisons.comparison: Both Microsoft and JPMorgan define the allowance for credit losses as representing management's estimate of expected credit losses over the life of the instrument (or remaining expected life). Both disclosures explicitly include financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain off-balance sheet lending-related commitments within the scope of this allowance.
